title.zh: 卷十九 梁書19: 列傳九 氏叔琮 朱友恭 王重師 朱珍 李思安 鄧季筠 黃文靖 胡規 李讜 李重胤 范居實
title.en: Volume 19 Book of Later Liang 19: Biographies 9 - Shi Shucong, Zhu Yougong, Wang Zhongshi, Zhu Zhen, Li Si'an, Deng Jiyun, Huang Wenjing, Hu Gui, Li Dang, Li Zhongyin, Fan Jushi
title.raw: 卷十九 梁書19: 列傳九 氏叔琮 朱友恭 王重師 朱珍 李思安 鄧季筠 黃文靖 胡規 李讜 李重胤 范居實 Volume 19 Book of Later Liang 19: Biographies 9 - Shi Shucong, Zhu Yougong, Wang Zhongshi, Zhu Zhen, Li Si'an, Deng Jiyun, Huang Wenjing, Hu Gui, Li Dang, Li Zhongyin, Fan Jushi

sentences.zh: 氏叔琮，尉氏人也。

translations.literal: Shi Shucong was a native of Weishi.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Shucong came from Weishi.

sentences.zh: 唐中和末，應募為騎軍，初隸於龐師古，為伍長。

translations.literal: At the end of Tang Zhonghe he answered the levy as cavalry, first attached to Pang Shigu as squad chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the last years of Zhonghe he joined the cavalry under Pang Shigu as a squad leader.

sentences.zh: 叔琮壯勇沈毅，膽力過人。

translations.literal: Shucong was stalwart, brave, and deep-steady; in daring and strength he surpassed others.
translations.idiomatic: Shucong was burly, brave, and steady; none matched his nerve.

sentences.zh: 太祖討巢、蔡於陳、許間，叔琮奮擊，首出諸校，太祖壯之，自行伍間擢為後院馬軍都將。

translations.literal: When the Founder campaigned against Chao and Cai between Chen and Xu, Shucong struck hard and led all the officers; the Founder admired him and from the ranks promoted him rear-courtyard horse-army commander.
translations.idiomatic: Fighting Huang Chao and Qin Zongquan between Chen and Xu, Shucong led the charge; the Founder pulled him from the ranks to command the rear-guard cavalry.

sentences.zh: 時東伐徐、鄆，多曆年所，叔琮身當矢石，奮不顧命，觀者許焉。

translations.literal: When the eastern campaign against Xu and Yan spanned many years, Shucong met arrows and stones in person, striving without regard for life—onlookers approved.
translations.idiomatic: Years of war in Xu and Yan saw Shucong take every blow without flinching; men who watched approved.

sentences.zh: 累遷為指揮使，尋奏授宿州刺史、檢校右僕射。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to commander; soon memorialized and appointed Suzhou prefect and acting Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to commander, then to Suzhou prefect and acting Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 太祖伐襄陽，叔琮失利，降為陽翟鎮遏使；

translations.literal: When the Founder attacked Xiangyang Shucong was defeated and demoted to Yangzhai frontier suppression commissioner;
translations.idiomatic: After a defeat at Xiangyang the Founder reduced him to frontier commissioner at Yangzhai;

sentences.zh: 尋又捍禦晉軍於洹水有功，遷曹州刺史。

translations.literal: soon after defending against Jin troops at the Huan River with merit, he was moved to Cao prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he held the Jin army at the Huan and was made prefect of Cao.

sentences.zh: 天復元年春，領大軍攻拔澤、潞，叔琮遂引兵北掠太原。

translations.literal: In spring of Tianfu year 1 he led a great army to capture Ze and Lu; Shucong then led troops north to raid Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Spring of Tianfu 1, the great army took Ze and Lu; Shucong marched north to raid Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 師還，除晉州節度使。

translations.literal: When the army returned he was made Jinzhou military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On the return he received Jinzhou as his command.

sentences.zh: 明年，太祖屯軍於岐下，晉軍潛襲絳州，前軍不利。

translations.literal: The next year the Founder encamped below Qi; Jin troops secretly raided Jiangzhou and the vanguard fared ill.
translations.idiomatic: Next year, with the Founder at Qi, Jin struck Jiang by stealth and the van was beaten.

sentences.zh: 晉軍恃勝攻臨汾，叔琮嚴設備禦。

translations.literal: Jin troops relying on victory attacked Linfen; Shucong strictly set defenses.
translations.idiomatic: Emboldened by victory, the Jin army moved on Linfen; Shucong fortified every approach.

sentences.zh: 乃於軍中選壯士二人，深目虯須，貌如沙陀者，令就襄陵縣牧馬於道間。

translations.literal: He then chose from the army two stalwart men, deep-eyed with curly beards, in appearance like Shatuo, and ordered them to pasture horses by the road near Xiangling county.
translations.idiomatic: He picked two broad-shouldered men with deep eyes, curling beards, and Shatuo looks, and set them to graze horses on the road near Xiangling.

sentences.zh: 蕃寇見之不疑，二人因雜其行間，俄而伺隙各擒一人而來。

translations.literal: Barbarian raiders seeing them did not doubt; the two mingled in their ranks and presently each seized one man and came back.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders took no alarm; the two slipped among them and, seizing their chance, each dragged back a prisoner.

sentences.zh: 晉軍大驚，且疑有伏兵，遂退據蒲縣。

translations.literal: Jin troops were greatly alarmed and suspected an ambush, so they withdrew to hold Pu county.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin host panicked at the thought of ambush and fell back to Pu county.

sentences.zh: 時太祖遣朱友寧將兵數萬赴應，悉委叔琮節制。

translations.literal: At that time the Founder sent Zhu Youning with tens of thousands of troops to assist and wholly entrusted command to Shucong.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder sent Zhu Youning with an army of tens of thousands and gave Shucong full command.

sentences.zh: 既至，諸將皆欲休軍，叔琮曰：「若然，則賊必遁矣，遁則何功焉！

translations.literal: When they arrived all the generals wished to rest the army; Shucong said: "If so, the bandits will surely flee—what merit if they flee!
translations.idiomatic: Once there, every general wanted rest; Shucong said, "Do that and they will run—and what glory is there in that?

sentences.zh: 」因夜出，潛師截其歸路，遇晉軍遊騎數百，盡殺之；

translations.literal: " Thereupon by night he went out, secretly sent troops to cut their line of retreat, met several hundred Jin patrol horse, and killed them all;
translations.idiomatic: " That night he stole out, cut their retreat, and slaughtered several hundred Jin scouts;

sentences.zh: 遂攻其壘，拔之，斬獲萬餘眾，奪馬三百匹。

translations.literal: then attacked their fort, took it, beheaded and captured over ten thousand, and seized three hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: then stormed their camp, took it, killed or captured more than ten thousand, and seized three hundred horses.

sentences.zh: 太祖聞之，喜謂左右曰：「殺蕃賊，破太原，非氏老不可！

translations.literal: The Founder heard and joyfully told his attendants: "To kill the barbarian bandits and break Taiyuan—none but Old Shi will do!
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the Founder he told his staff, "To kill these barbarians and break Taiyuan we need none but Old Shi!

sentences.zh: 」叔琮乃長驅收汾州，與晉人轉戰，直抵並壘。

translations.literal: " Shucong then drove far to recover Fenzhou, fought in turn with the Jin, and straight to the walls of Bing.
translations.idiomatic: " Shucong drove on to recover Fenzhou, traded blows with the Jin all the way to the walls of Bing.

sentences.zh: 軍回，以其功奏加檢校司空。

translations.literal: When the army returned, his merit was memorialized and he was given acting Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return his deeds won him acting Grand Master of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 自後累年，晉軍不敢侵軼。

translations.literal: From then for accumulated years Jin troops did not dare invade or raid.
translations.idiomatic: For years after, the Jin army did not dare cross the border.

sentences.zh: 叔琮養士愛民，甚有能政。

translations.literal: Shucong nourished scholar-officers and loved the people; he had quite able governance.
translations.idiomatic: Shucong kept good men close and cared for the people; his rule was capable.

sentences.zh: 天復三年，為鄜州留後，尋真領保大軍節度使、檢校司徒。

translations.literal: In Tianfu year 3 he was made Minzhou regent and soon truly held Baoda army military governor and acting Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianfu 3 he became regent at Min, then full military governor of Baoda with acting Grand Tutor rank.

sentences.zh: 及昭宗東遷，征為右龍虎統軍，以衛洛陽。

translations.literal: When Zhaozong moved east he was summoned as Right Dragon-Tiger commander to guard Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhaozong moved east, Shucong was called to guard Luoyang as commander of the Right Dragon-Tiger Guard.

sentences.zh: 天祐元年八月，與朱友恭同受太祖密旨，弑昭宗於大內。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of Tianyou year 1 he with Zhu Yougong together received the Founder's secret order and assassinated Zhaozong in the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Tianyou 1 he and Zhu Yougong, on the Founder's secret order, killed Zhaozong inside the palace.

sentences.zh: 既而責以軍政不理，貶白州司戶。

translations.literal: Soon after he was charged with disorder in military government and demoted to Baizhou registrar.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was blamed for slack command and demoted to registrar at Baizhou.

sentences.zh: 尋賜自盡。

translations.literal: Before long he was granted suicide.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly thereafter he was ordered to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 叔琮將死，呼曰：「賣我性命，欲塞天下之謗，其如神理何！

translations.literal: As Shucong was about to die he cried: "You sell my life to plug the world's blame—what of divine principle!
translations.idiomatic: Facing death Shucong cried, "You sell my life to silence the world—what of heaven's judgment!

sentences.zh: 」乾化二年，詔許歸葬。

translations.literal: " In Qianhua year 2 an edict permitted return for burial.
translations.idiomatic: " In Qianhua 2 an edict allowed his body to be brought home for burial.

sentences.zh: 朱友恭，壽春人，本姓李，名彥威。

translations.literal: Zhu Yougong, a man of Shouchun, originally surnamed Li and named Yanwei.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yougong came from Shouchun; his birth name was Li Yanwei.

sentences.zh: 瑽角事太祖，性穎利，善體太祖意，太祖憐之，因畜為己子，賜姓，初名克讓，後改之。

translations.literal: From boyhood he served the Founder; nature keen and clever, good at grasping the Founder's intent—the Founder pitied him and therefore raised him as his own son, granting the surname; first named Kerang, later changed.
translations.idiomatic: A boy in the Founder's service, clever and quick to read his mood, he was adopted, given the Zhu surname, first Kerang, then Yougong.

sentences.zh: 時初建左長劍都，以友恭董之。

translations.literal: When the Left Long-Sword Corps was first established, Yougong was put in charge.
translations.idiomatic: When the Left Long-Sword Corps was formed, Yougong was placed at its head.

sentences.zh: 從太祖四征，稍立軍功，累遷諸軍都指揮使、檢校左僕射。

translations.literal: Following the Founder on four campaigns he gradually achieved military merit, repeatedly promoted to all-armies commander and acting Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Four campaigns with the Founder won him steady promotions to army commander and acting Left Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 乾寧中，授汝州刺史，加檢校司空。

translations.literal: In the Qianning years he was appointed Ruzhou prefect and added acting Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qianning he became prefect of Ru with acting Grand Master rank.

sentences.zh: 光化初，淮夷侵鄂渚，武昌帥杜洪來乞師，太祖遣友恭將兵萬餘，濟江應援，引兵至龍沙、九江而還，軍聲大振。

translations.literal: Early Guanghua, Huaiyi invaded E's shallows; Wuchang commander Du Hong came begging troops; the Founder sent Yougong with over ten thousand troops across the river to aid, led troops to Longsha and Jiujiang and returned—the army's fame greatly shook.
translations.idiomatic: Early Guanghua, when Huainan raiders struck Ezhou, Du Hong of Wuchang begged help; Yougong crossed the Yangzi with ten thousand men, swept to Longsha and Jiujiang, and returned to thunderous reputation.

sentences.zh: 時淮寇據黃州，友恭攻陷其壁，獲賊將瞿章，俘斬萬計。

translations.literal: At that time Huai bandits held Huangzhou; Yougong stormed their fortress, captured bandit commander Qu Zhang, prisoners beheaded numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: He stormed Huangzhou, took the rebel Qu Zhang, and killed or captured ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 途經安陸，因襲殺刺史武瑜，盡收其眾，以功為潁州刺史，加檢校司徒。

translations.literal: Passing through Anlu he thereupon raided and killed prefect Wu Yu, wholly gathered his troops, and for merit was made Yingzhou prefect with acting Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Passing Anlu he killed Prefect Wu Yu, absorbed his troops, and for that deed was made prefect of Ying with acting Grand Tutor rank.

sentences.zh: 天復中，為武寧軍留後。

translations.literal: In Tianfu he was made Wuning army regent.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianfu he served as regent of Wuning.

sentences.zh: 天祐初，昭宗東遷洛邑，征拜左龍虎統軍，以衛宮闕。

translations.literal: Early Tianyou, Zhaozong moved east to Luoyi; summoned as Left Dragon-Tiger commander to guard the palace gates.
translations.idiomatic: Early Tianyou, when Zhaozong moved to Luoyang, Yougong was called to guard the palace as Left Dragon-Tiger commander.

sentences.zh: 尋與氏叔琮同受太祖密旨，弑昭宗於洛陽宮。

translations.literal: Soon with Shi Shucong he together received the Founder's secret order and assassinated Zhaozong at Luoyang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he and Shi Shucong, on the same secret order, killed Zhaozong in the Luoyang palace.

sentences.zh: 既而太祖自河中至，責以慢於軍政，貶崖州司戶，復其本姓名，與氏叔琮同日賜死。

translations.literal: Soon the Founder came from Hezhong, charged him with laxity in military government, demoted to Yazhou registrar, restored his original surname and name, and on the same day as Shi Shucong granted death.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder came from Hezhong he accused Yougong of negligence, stripped him to registrar at Yazhou, restored the name Li Yanwei, and had him executed the same day as Shucong.

sentences.zh: 王重師，潁州長社人也。

translations.literal: Wang Chongshi was a native of Changshe in Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chongshi came from Changshe in Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 材力兼人，沈嘿大度，臨事有權變，劍槊之妙，冠絕於一時。

translations.literal: In talent and strength he matched many men; deep, silent, and great-minded; facing affairs he had timely expedients; in spear and halberd skill he crowned the age.
translations.idiomatic: Strong as three men, quiet and broad-minded, quick with expedients in crisis, his spear-work was unmatched in his day.

sentences.zh: 唐中和末，蔡寇陷許昌，重師脫身而來，太祖異其狀貌，乃隸於拔山都。

translations.literal: At the end of Tang Zhonghe Cai bandits took Xuchang; Chongshi escaped and came; the Founder marveled at his appearance and attached him to the Uproot-Mountains Corps.
translations.idiomatic: When Cai rebels seized Xuchang at the end of Zhonghe, Chongshi broke free and fled to the Founder, who marveled at him and enrolled him in the Mount Uprooted Corps.

sentences.zh: 每於軍前效用，頗出儕類。

translations.literal: Whenever he served before the army he quite surpassed his peers.
translations.idiomatic: In action he always outshone his fellows.

sentences.zh: 文德中，令董左右長劍軍。

translations.literal: In the Wende years he was ordered to direct the Left and Right Long-Sword armies.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wende he took charge of the Left and Right Long-Sword armies.

sentences.zh: 太祖伐上蔡，重師力戰有功。

translations.literal: When the Founder attacked Shangcai, Chongshi fought hard with merit.
translations.idiomatic: At Shangcai he fought with distinguished valor.

sentences.zh: 及討兗、鄆，擢為指揮使，奏授檢校右僕射。

translations.literal: When campaigning against Yan and Yanzhou he was promoted to commander and memorialized as acting Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yan and Yan campaigns he rose to commander and acting Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 重師枕戈擐甲五六年，於齊、魯間凡經百餘戰，由是威震敵人。

translations.literal: Chongshi slept on his spear and buckled armor five or six years; between Qi and Lu he passed through altogether more than a hundred battles—thereby his awe shook the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: For five or six years he slept in armor; between Qi and Lu he fought more than a hundred battles until the enemy feared his name.

sentences.zh: 尋授檢校司空，為潁州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon appointed acting Grand Master and made Yingzhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made acting Grand Master and prefect of Ying.

sentences.zh: 乾寧中，太祖攻濮州，縱兵壞其墉，濮人因屯火塞其壞壘，煙焰亙空，人莫敢越。

translations.literal: In Qianning the Founder attacked Puzhou, sent troops to break its wall; Pu people heaped fire to block the breach, smoke and flame spanning the sky, and none dared cross.
translations.idiomatic: At Puzhou in Qianning the breach was made, but defenders piled fire in the gap until smoke blotted the sky and no man would cross.

sentences.zh: 重師方苦金瘡，臥於軍次，諸將或勉之，乃躍起，命壯士悉取軍中氈罽投水中，擲於火上，重師然後率精銳，持短兵突入，諸軍踵之，濮州乃陷。

translations.literal: Chongshi was then suffering a metal wound, lying in the army camp; generals sometimes urged him—he then leaped up, ordered stalwarts to take all the army's felt blankets and throw them in water and onto the fire; Chongshi then led crack troops with short weapons bursting in; the armies followed—and Puzhou fell.
translations.idiomatic: Wounded, he lay in camp until his officers roused him; he leaped up, had men soak felt and fling it on the flames, then led elite troops with short blades through the gap—the army poured after and Puzhou fell.

sentences.zh: 重師為劍槊所傷，身被八九創，丁壯荷之還營，且將斃矣。

translations.literal: Chongshi was wounded by spear and halberd, his body bearing eight or nine cuts; strong youths carried him back to camp—he was near death.
translations.idiomatic: Spears left eight or nine wounds; bearers carried him back half dead.

sentences.zh: 太祖驚惜尤甚，曰：「雖得濮壘，而失重師，奈何！

translations.literal: The Founder was startled and grieved beyond measure, saying: "Though we have taken the Pu fortress, we have lost Chongshi—what is to be done!
translations.idiomatic: The Founder was stricken: "We have Puzhou but may lose Chongshi—what then!

sentences.zh: 」亟命以奇藥療之，彌月始愈。

translations.literal: " He at once ordered extraordinary medicines to treat him; a full month passed before recovery.
translations.idiomatic: " He sent rare drugs; a full month passed before Chongshi could rise.

sentences.zh: 尋知平盧軍留後，加檢校司徒。

translations.literal: Soon made acting Pinglu army regent and added acting Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made regent of Pinglu with acting Grand Tutor rank.

sentences.zh: 其後北伐幽、滄、鎮、定，屢與晉軍接戰，頗得士心，故多勝捷。

translations.literal: Afterward on northern expeditions to You, Cang, Zhen, and Ding he repeatedly met Jin troops in battle, quite won soldiers' hearts, and therefore had many victories.
translations.idiomatic: Northern campaigns against You, Cang, Zhen, and Ding brought repeated clashes with Jin; he won his men's hearts and many victories.

sentences.zh: 天祐中，授雍州節度使，加同平章事。

translations.literal: In Tianyou appointed Yongzhou military governor and added Honorary Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianyou he became military governor of Yongzhou and Honorary Councilor.

sentences.zh: 數年治戎恤民，頗有威惠。

translations.literal: For several years governing the army and cherishing the people, he had quite awe and kindness.
translations.idiomatic: For years he drilled the army and cared for the people; awe and kindness attended his rule.

sentences.zh: 開平中，為劉捍所構，太祖深疑之，然未有以發其事。

translations.literal: In Kaiping he was framed by Liu Han; the Founder deeply suspected him, yet had no means to raise the matter.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiping Liu Han slandered him; the Founder grew suspicious but lacked cause to act.

sentences.zh: 無何，擅遣裨將張君練縱兵深入邠、鳳，君練敗北。

translations.literal: Before long he on his own authority sent lieutenant Zhang Junlian to lead troops deep into Bin and Feng; Junlian was defeated and fled north.
translations.idiomatic: Then, without leave, he sent Zhang Junlian raiding into Bin and Feng; Junlian was routed.

sentences.zh: 太祖聞之，怒其專擅，因追而斬之。

translations.literal: The Founder heard, was angry at his willful authority, and pursued and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of it, the Founder raged at his insubordination, overtook him, and beheaded him.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note on Wang Chongshi from the 《Zizhi Tongjian》:
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note on Wang Chongshi from the 《Zizhi Tongjian》:

sentences.zh: （《通鑒》云劉捍至長安，王重師不為禮，捍譖之帝，曰：「重師潛與邠、岐通。

translations.literal: (The 《Comprehensive Mirror》 says: When Liu Han reached Chang'an, Wang Chongshi did not show courtesy; Han slandered him to the Emperor, saying: "Chongshi secretly communicates with Bin and Qi.
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Zizhi Tongjian》 says Liu Han reached Chang'an and Chongshi refused him courtesy; Han told the Emperor, "Chongshi is in secret contact with Bin and Qi.

sentences.zh: 」甲申，貶溪州刺史，尋賜自盡，夷其族。）〉

translations.literal: " On jiashen he was demoted to Xizhou prefect; soon granted suicide and his clan exterminated.）〉
translations.idiomatic: " On jiashen he was demoted to Xi, then ordered to die; his clan was destroyed.）〉

sentences.zh: 朱珍，徐州豐縣雍鳳里人也。

translations.literal: Zhu Zhen was a man of Yongfeng lane, Feng county, Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Zhen came from Yongfeng lane in Feng county, Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 太祖初起兵，珍與龐師古、許唐、李暉、丁會、氏叔琮、鄧季筠、王武等八十餘人，以中涓從，摧堅陷陣，所向蕩決。

translations.literal: When the Founder first raised troops, Zhen with Pang Shigu, Xu Tang, Li Hui, Ding Hui, Shi Shucong, Deng Jiyun, Wang Wu, and more than eighty others followed as personal attendants—overthrowing strongholds and smashing battle arrays, wherever they aimed swept away.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder first took up arms, Zhen and more than eighty comrades—including Pang Shigu, Xu Tang, Li Hui, Ding Hui, Shi Shucong, Deng Jiyun, and Wang Wu—rode at his side and broke every line they met.

sentences.zh: 及太祖鎮汴，兼領招討使，署珍為宣武右職，以總腹心。

translations.literal: When the Founder held Bian and concurrently led the punitive commissioner, he appointed Zhen to Xuanwu right duties to oversee the inner circle.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder held Bian as punitive commissioner, he made Zhen his right hand at Xuanwu to command his trusted men.

sentences.zh: 於是簡練軍伍，裁制綱紀，平巢破蔡，多珍之力也。

translations.literal: Thereupon he selected and drilled the army host, trimmed and set regulations—pacifying Chao and breaking Cai owed much to Zhen's strength.
translations.idiomatic: He drilled the ranks and enforced discipline; much of the victory over Chao and Cai was Zhen's doing.

sentences.zh: 始尚讓以驍騎五千人至繁臺，珍與龐師古、齊奉國等擊退之。

translations.literal: At first Shang Rang came with five thousand fierce cavalry to Fantai; Zhen with Pang Shigu, Qi Fengguo, and others drove him back.
translations.idiomatic: When Shang Rang brought five thousand horsemen to Fantai, Zhen, Pang Shigu, and Qi Fengguo beat them back.

sentences.zh: 及黃巢敗，珍與並帥李克用追至冤句而還。

translations.literal: When Bing's Huang Chao was defeated, Zhen with Bing commander Li Keyong pursued to Yuanqu and returned.
translations.idiomatic: After Huang Chao's defeat Zhen pursued with Li Keyong of Bing as far as Yuanqu, then turned back.

sentences.zh: 尋從太祖以汴、宋、亳之師入西華，破王夏寨，勇冠軍鋒，以功加秩。

translations.literal: Soon following the Founder with Bian, Song, and Bo troops into Xihua, he broke Wang Xia's stockade, courage crowning the army's point—for merit rank was added.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the Founder into Xihua with armies from Bian, Song, and Bo, stormed Wang Xia's camp, led the van in valor, and won higher rank.

sentences.zh: 光啟元年，署諸軍都指揮使，始為上將。

translations.literal: Guangqi year 1, appointed all-armies commander—first becoming a senior general.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangqi 1 he became army commander—a full general at last.

sentences.zh: 於是軍焦夷，敗蔡師鐵林三千人，盡俘其將。

translations.literal: Thereupon the army was at Jiaoyi, defeated three thousand Iron Forest troops of Cai army, wholly captured their generals.
translations.idiomatic: At Jiaoyi he smashed three thousand Iron Forest Guards of the Cai army and took every officer prisoner.

sentences.zh: 復西至汝、鄭，南過陳、潁，繚宋、亳、滑、濮間，與蔡賊交戰，鏖伏襲殺，不知其數。

translations.literal: Again west to Ru and Zheng, south past Chen and Ying, winding among Song, Bo, Hua, and Pu—battling Cai bandits in grinding fights, ambushes, and killings beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: West to Ru and Zheng, south through Chen and Ying, he ranged Song, Bo, Hua, and Pu fighting Cai rebels in ambush after battle beyond count.

sentences.zh: 會滑州節度使安師儒戎政不治，太祖命珍與李唐賓率步騎以經略之。

translations.literal: When Huazhou military governor An Shiru had disorderly military government, the Founder ordered Zhen with Li Tangbin to lead foot and horse to take it in hand.
translations.idiomatic: When An Shiru of Huazhou misgoverned his command, the Founder sent Zhen and Li Tangbin to seize the province.

sentences.zh: 始入境，遇大雪，令軍士無得休息，一夕馳至壁下，百梯並升，遂乘其墉，滑州平。

translations.literal: Just entering the border they met great snow; he ordered soldiers not to rest—one night galloped to below the wall, a hundred ladders rose together, then mounted the rampart, and Huazhou was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Snow met them at the border; he allowed no halt. In one night they were at the walls, a hundred ladders went up together, and Huazhou fell.

sentences.zh: 時太祖方謀齊師，乃遣珍往淄州募兵，行次任縣，東面都統齊克讓伏兵於孫師陂以邀珍，珍大破之。

translations.literal: At that time the Founder was planning Qi armies and sent Zhen to Zizhou to raise troops; passing Ren county, Eastern Front commander Qi Kerang lay in ambush at Sunshi Slope to intercept Zhen—Zhen greatly defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: While the Founder planned against Qi, Zhen went to Zizhou to raise troops; Qi Kerang ambushed him at Sunshi Slope near Ren county—Zhen broke him utterly.

sentences.zh: 進軍至牙山，都虞候張仁遇白珍曰：「軍有不齊者，當先斬本都將，後以狀聞，願許之。

translations.literal: Advancing to Yashan, ward-inspector Zhang Renyu reported to Zhen: "When the army is out of step, first behead that unit's commander, then report by memorial—I beg permission.
translations.idiomatic: At Yashan, Inspector Zhang Renyu asked Zhen: "When a unit falters, let me kill its commander first and report after—grant me that right.

sentences.zh: 」珍怒其專，乃斬仁遇以徇軍，由是諸將咸懼。

translations.literal: " Zhen was angry at his presumption, beheaded Renyu to warn the army, and thereby all generals feared.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhen, furious at the presumption, executed Renyu before the ranks, and every officer thereafter lived in fear.

sentences.zh: 兵至乾封，與淄人戰於白草口，敗之。

translations.literal: Troops reached Qianfeng and fought Qi men at Baicao Mouth—defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: At Qianfeng he met the Qi army at Baicao Mouth and routed them.

sentences.zh: 青人以步騎二萬，列三寨於金嶺驛，珍與戰，連破之，殲其師，盡獲軍器戎馬。

translations.literal: Qing men with twenty thousand foot and horse set three camps at Jinling Post; Zhen fought them, repeatedly broke them, annihilated their army, and wholly seized weapons and war horses.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty thousand Qi troops held three camps at Jinling Post; Zhen broke them in succession, destroyed the army, and took all arms and horses.

sentences.zh: 是夕，攻博昌，大獲兵眾。

translations.literal: That night he attacked Bochang and greatly gained troops.
translations.idiomatic: That night he stormed Bochang and swelled his ranks with captives.

sentences.zh: 其後破盧瑭、張至及朱瑄、朱瑾之眾，平定曹、濮，未嘗不在戰中。

translations.literal: Afterward he broke the hosts of Lu Tang, Zhang Zhi, Zhu Xuan, and Zhu Jin, pacified Cao and Pu—never absent from battle.
translations.idiomatic: He fought Lu Tang, Zhang Zhi, Zhu Xuan, and Zhu Jin, pacified Cao and Pu, and was never far from the fighting.

sentences.zh: 梁山之役，始與李唐賓不協。

translations.literal: In the battle at Liangshan he first fell out with Li Tangbin.
translations.idiomatic: At Liangshan he first clashed with Li Tangbin.

sentences.zh: 珍在軍嘗私迎其室於汴，而不先請，太祖疑之，密令唐賓察之，二將不相下，因而交諍。

translations.literal: Zhen in the army once privately welcomed his household to Bian without asking first; the Founder suspected this and secretly ordered Tangbin to observe— the two generals would not yield, and thus quarreled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen had his wife brought to Bian without permission; the Founder suspected collusion and set Tangbin to watch—the two generals quarreled and would not yield.

sentences.zh: 唐賓夜斬關還汴以訴，珍亦棄軍單騎而至，太祖兩惜之，故不罪，俾還於師。

translations.literal: Tangbin by night cut the pass and returned to Bian to complain; Zhen too abandoned the army and came alone on horseback; the Founder cherished both and therefore did not punish, ordering them back to the army.
translations.idiomatic: Tangbin broke through at night to complain at Bian; Zhen rode alone from the camp; the Founder valued both and sent them back without punishment.

sentences.zh: 復以踏白騎士入陳、亳間，以邀蔡人，遂南至斤溝，破淮西石璠之師二萬，擄璠以獻。

translations.literal: Again with scout cavalry he entered between Chen and Bo to intercept Cai men, then south to Jingou, broke Huaixi Shi Fan's army of twenty thousand, and captured Fan to present.
translations.idiomatic: With scout horse he raided between Chen and Bo, drove south to Jingou, shattered Shi Fan's twenty thousand Huai troops, and brought Fan in chains.

sentences.zh: 珍旋師自亳北趣靜戎，濟舟於滑，破黎陽、臨河、李固三鎮。

translations.literal: Zhen wheeled the army from north of Bo toward Jingrong, crossed boats at Hua, and broke the three garrisons of Liyang, Linhe, and Ligu.
translations.idiomatic: Turning north from Bo toward Jingrong, he crossed the river at Hua and took Liyang, Linhe, and Ligu.

sentences.zh: 軍於內黃，敗樂從訓萬餘人，分命聶金、範居實略澶州，與魏師遇於臨黃；

translations.literal: Army at Neihuang defeated Yue Congxun's more than ten thousand, separately ordered Nie Jin and Fan Jushi to take Caozhou, met Wei army at Linhuang;
translations.idiomatic: At Neihuang he beat Yue Congxun's ten thousand, sent Nie Jin and Fan Jushi against Caozhou, and met the Wei army at Linhuang;

sentences.zh: 魏軍有豹子軍二千人，戮之無噍類，威振河朔。

translations.literal: Wei army had two thousand Leopard Corps—slaughtered to the last mouthful; awe shook Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: He slaughtered the two thousand Leopard Guards to the last man, and his name shook the north.

sentences.zh: 復攻淮西，至蔡，夾河而寨，敗賊將蕭皓之眾，皆擁於河溺死之。

translations.literal: Again attacked Huaixi, reached Cai, camped on both sides of the river, defeated bandit commander Xiao Hao's host—all were crowded into the river and drowned.
translations.idiomatic: Again in Huaixi he reached Cai, camped along both banks of the river, routed Xiao Hao's rebels, and drove them into the water to drown.

sentences.zh: 進軍蔡州，營其西南，既破羊馬垣，遇雨班師。

translations.literal: Advanced on Caizhou, camped southwest, having broken sheep-and-horse rampart met rain and withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: He besieged Caizhou from the southwest, broke the outer rampart, then withdrew in the rain.

sentences.zh: 珍以兵援劉讚，赴楚州，至襄山南，遇徐戎扼其路，珍乃攻豐，下之。

translations.literal: Zhen with troops aided Liu Zan, went to Chuzhou, reached south of Xiangshan, met Xu troops blocking the road—Zhen then attacked Feng and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Marching to aid Liu Zan at Chuzhou, he found Xu troops blocking the road south of Xiangshan and took Feng by storm.

sentences.zh: 時溥乃以全師會戰於豐南吳康裏，珍乃收豐，破其三萬餘眾。

translations.literal: Shi Pu then with full army joined battle at Wukang li south of Feng—Zhen secured Feng and broke his more than thirty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Pu met him with his full army at Wukang li south of Feng; Zhen held the city and shattered thirty thousand.

sentences.zh: 及蔡賊平，珍比諸將功居多。

translations.literal: When Cai bandits were pacified, Zhen compared with other generals had the greater share of merit.
translations.idiomatic: When Cai fell, his share of the credit exceeded every other general.

sentences.zh: 龍紀初，與諸將屯於蕭縣，以禦時溥，珍慮太祖自至，令諸軍葺馬廄以候巡撫，李唐賓之裨將嚴郊獨慢焉，軍候範權恃珍以督之。

translations.literal: Early Longji, with generals he garrisoned at Xiaoxian to oppose Shi Pu; Zhen feared the Founder would come in person, ordered all armies to repair horse stables to await inspection; Li Tangbin's lieutenant Yan Jiao alone was slack; army scout Fan Quan relied on Zhen to supervise.
translations.idiomatic: Early Longji he held Xiaoxian against Shi Pu; expecting the Founder's inspection, Zhen ordered every unit to rebuild its stables; Yan Jiao, Tangbin's lieutenant, alone was slack, and Fan Quan, backed by Zhen, pressed him.

sentences.zh: 唐賓素與珍不協，果怒，乃見以訴其事。

translations.literal: Tangbin had long been at odds with Zhen; as expected he was angry, then went in audience to complain of the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Tangbin had long hated Zhen; predictably furious, he went to the Founder to complain.

sentences.zh: 珍亦怒曰：「唐賓無禮！

translations.literal: Zhen also angrily said: "Tangbin is rude!
translations.idiomatic: Zhen snapped: "Tangbin has no manners!

sentences.zh: 」遂拔劍斬之，珍命騎列狀陳其事。

translations.literal: 」Then he drew his sword and slew him; Zhen ordered the cavalry to file a report stating the matter.
translations.idiomatic: 」 He drew his sword and killed him, then had the cavalry file a report on what had happened.

sentences.zh: 太祖初聞唐賓之死，驚駭，與敬翔謀，詐令有司收捕唐賓妻子下獄，以安珍心。

translations.literal: When the Founder first heard of Tangbin's death he was alarmed; with Jing Xiang he plotted to have officials falsely arrest Tangbin's wife and children and imprison them to reassure Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder first heard Tangbin was dead he was shocked; with Jing Xiang he pretended to arrest Tangbin's family to calm Zhen.

sentences.zh: 太祖遂徑往蕭縣，距蕭一舍，珍率將校迎謁，梁祖令武士執之，責其專殺，命丁會行戮。

translations.literal: The Founder went straight to Xiao county; one stage from Xiao, Zhen led the generals to welcome him; the Liang Founder had warriors seize him, blamed him for unauthorized killing, and ordered Ding Hui to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder rode straight to Xiao county; a stage short of the city Zhen came out with his officers to greet him; the Liang Founder had guards seize him, blamed him for killing on his own authority, and ordered Ding Hui to carry out the sentence.

sentences.zh: 都將霍存等數十人叩頭以救，太祖怒，以坐床擲之，乃退。

translations.literal: Several dozen commanders including Huo Cun knocked their heads to plead for him; the Founder in anger threw his couch at them, and they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Several dozen commanders led by Huo Cun kowtowed to beg for his life; the Founder in rage hurled his couch at them, and they fell back.

sentences.zh: 李思安，陳留張亭里人也。

translations.literal: Li Si'an was a native of Zhangting hamlet in Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Si'an came from Zhangting in Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 初事汴將楊彥洪為騎士。

translations.literal: At first he served Bian general Yang Yanhong as a cavalryman.
translations.idiomatic: He first served Yang Yanhong of Bian as a horse soldier.

sentences.zh: 好拳勇，未弱冠，長七尺，超然有乘時自奮之意。

translations.literal: He loved fists and valor; before his cap was grown he stood seven feet, with surpassing ambition to seize the moment and exert himself.
translations.idiomatic: Fond of boxing and daring, he was seven feet tall before manhood and burned to make his mark in the world.

sentences.zh: 唐中和三年，太祖鎮汴，嘗大閱戎旅，睹其材，甚偉之，因錫名思安，字貞臣。

translations.literal: Tang Zhonghe 3, the Founder held Bian; at a great review of the army he saw his talent, greatly admired him, and bestowed the name Si'an, style Zhenchen.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhonghe 3 of Tang, when the Founder held Bian he reviewed the troops, admired his build, and gave him the name Si'an, styled Zhenchen.

sentences.zh: 思安善飛槊，所向披靡，每從太祖征伐，常馳馬出敵陣之後，測其厚薄而還。

translations.literal: Si'an was skilled with the flying lance; wherever he went none could stand; each time he followed the Founder in campaigns he would often gallop out behind the enemy lines, gauge their strength, and return.
translations.idiomatic: Si'an wielded the flying lance to devastating effect and often rode alone behind enemy lines to test their strength before returning.

sentences.zh: 或敵人有恃猛自炫者，多命取之，必鷹揚飆卷，擒馘於萬眾之中，出入自若，如蹈無人之地。

translations.literal: When enemies had fierce men who relied on their might to show off, he was often ordered to take them; he must soar like an eagle in the gale and capture heads in the midst of ten thousand—entering and leaving as if treading where no man was.
translations.idiomatic: When the foe put forward swaggering champions, he was sent to take them—swooping through ten thousand men to seize heads and ride out as if the field were empty.

sentences.zh: 太祖甚惜之，命副王虔裕為踏白將。

translations.literal: The Founder prized him greatly and ordered him to assist Wang Qianyu as Tread-White commander.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder valued him and made him Wang Qianyu's deputy as Tread-White commander.

sentences.zh: 時巢、蔡合從，太祖每遣偵邏，必率先獨往。

translations.literal: When Chao and Cai allied, whenever the Founder sent scouts Si'an always went first alone.
translations.idiomatic: While Huang Chao and the Cai rebels were allied, Si'an always went ahead alone whenever the Founder sent scouts.

sentences.zh: 巢敗走，思安領所部百餘人追賊，殺戮掩奪，眾莫敢當。

translations.literal: When Chao was defeated and fled, Si'an led his command of over a hundred men in pursuit, slaying and seizing plunder—the masses did not dare stand against him.
translations.idiomatic: When Chao fled in defeat, Si'an led a hundred-odd men in pursuit, killing and looting until none dared face him.

sentences.zh: 尋領軍襲蔡寇於鄭，都將李唐賓馬躓而墜，思安援槊刺追者，唐賓復其騎而還。

translations.literal: Soon he led troops in a raid on Cai bandits at Zheng; commander Li Tangbin's horse stumbled and he fell; Si'an with his lance stabbed the pursuers and Tangbin remounted and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He later struck Cai rebels at Zheng; when Li Tangbin was thrown, Si'an speared the pursuers so Tangbin could remount and escape.

sentences.zh: 又嘗與蔡人鬥，當陣生擒賊將柳行實。

translations.literal: He also once fought Cai men in battle and in the front line personally captured the bandit general Liu Xingshi.
translations.idiomatic: In another fight with the Cai army he took their general Liu Xingshi alive in the front ranks.

sentences.zh: 其後渡長淮，下天長、高郵二邑，又拒孫儒，迫濠州，皆有奇績。

translations.literal: After that he crossed the Long Huai, took Tianchang and Gaoyou, and also resisted Sun Ru and pressed Chuzhou—all had strange merit.
translations.idiomatic: He then crossed the Huai, took Tianchang and Gaoyou, held off Sun Ru, and pressed Chuzhou—each exploit was remarkable.

sentences.zh: 累遷為諸軍都指揮使，奏官至檢校左僕射，尋拜亳州刺史。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to overall commander of the armies; memorialized to Acting Left Vice Director; soon made Bozhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to overall army commander and Acting Left Vice Director, then became prefect of Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 練兵禦寇，邊境肅然。

translations.literal: He drilled troops and guarded against bandits; the border was solemnly ordered.
translations.idiomatic: He trained troops and held the border; the frontier grew quiet.

sentences.zh: 思安為性勇悍，每統戎臨敵，不大勝，必大敗。

translations.literal: Si'an by nature was fierce and bold; whenever he commanded the army facing the enemy, if he did not win greatly he must lose greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Fierce by nature, Si'an in command either won a crushing victory or suffered a crushing defeat.

sentences.zh: 開平元年春，率兵伐幽州，營於桑乾河，擄獲甚眾，燕人大懼。

translations.literal: Kaiping 1 spring, he led troops to attack Youzhou; camped on the Sanggan River; captures were very many; Yan men greatly feared.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of Kaiping 1 he attacked Youzhou and camped on the Sanggan, taking many captives and terrifying the Yan.

sentences.zh: 及軍回，率諸軍伐潞，累月不克，師人多逸。

translations.literal: When the army returned he led the armies to attack Lu; for many months could not take it; many in the army deserted.
translations.idiomatic: On the return march he besieged Lu for months without success, and many soldiers deserted.

sentences.zh: 太祖怒甚，詔疏其罪，盡奪其官爵，委本郡以民戶係焉。

translations.literal: The Founder was greatly enraged; an edict listed his crimes; stripped all ranks and titles; relegated to the prefecture as civilian household attachment.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder was furious, published his crimes, stripped every rank, and bound him to his home prefecture as a common household.

sentences.zh: 逾歲起之，復令領兵，亦無巨績可紀。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was raised again, again ordered to lead troops—also no great achievement to record.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was recalled to lead troops again, but still won no great fame.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘗因命將授鉞，謂左右曰：「李思安當敵果敢，無出其右者，然每遇藩方擇材，吾將用之，則敗聞必至，如是者二三矣，則知飛將數奇，前史豈虛言哉！

translations.literal: The Founder once when appointing generals and granting axes said to those at his side: "Li Si'an facing the enemy is bold and decisive, none surpasses him; yet each time when a border region chooses talent I intend to use him, defeat news must arrive—so two or three times—then one knows the flying general's repeated odd fate; former histories were not empty words!
translations.idiomatic: Once, as he gave axes to his generals, the Founder told his attendants: "Li Si'an is matchless in a fight, yet whenever I post him to a frontier command defeat follows—two or three times now. The old books were right about unlucky flying generals!

sentences.zh: 」乾化元年秋，又以為相州刺史。

translations.literal: 」Kaiping 1 autumn, again made Xiangzhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: 」 In autumn of Kaiping 1 he was again made prefect of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 思安自謂當擁旄仗鉞，及是殊不快意，但日循晏安，無意為政。

translations.literal: Si'an thought he ought to hold the banner and battle-axe; at this he was especially displeased; he only daily followed peaceful ease, with no mind for governing.
translations.idiomatic: Si'an had expected a military commission; bitterly disappointed, he idled in comfort and ignored government.

sentences.zh: 及太祖北征，以候騎之誤，落然無所具，而復壁壘荒圮，帑廩空竭，太祖怒，貶柳州司戶，尋賜死於相州。

translations.literal: When the Founder went north on campaign, because of scout error he was suddenly without all preparations; walls and fortifications in ruins, treasury empty; the Founder was angry, demoted to Liuzhou registrar, soon ordered to die at Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On a northern campaign the Founder arrived unexpectedly; Si'an had nothing ready, his walls were broken, and his stores were bare. The Founder demoted him to Liuzhou registrar and soon had him executed at Xiangzhou.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note on Li Si'an from the 《Comprehensive Mirror》:
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note on Li Si'an from the 《Zizhi Tongjian》:

sentences.zh: （《通鑒》：開化元年丙午，至相州，刺史李思安不意帝猝至，落然無具，坐削官爵。

translations.literal: (The 《Comprehensive Mirror》 says: Kaikai 1 bingwu, arrived at Xiangzhou; prefect Li Si'an did not expect the Emperor's sudden arrival, was suddenly without all preparations, and was demoted in office and stripped of rank.
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Zizhi Tongjian》 says: In Kaiping 1, bingwu year, the Emperor reached Xiangzhou; Prefect Li Si'an, caught unprepared, was stripped of rank on the spot.

sentences.zh: 二年正月丁卯，帝至獲嘉，追思李思安去歲供饋有闕，貶柳州司戶，尋長流思安於崖州，賜死。）〉

translations.literal: Year 2 first month dingmao, the Emperor arrived at Huojia; recalling Li Si'an's last year provisions were lacking, demoted to Liuzhou registrar; soon exiled Si'an to Yazhou for life, ordered to die.)〉
translations.idiomatic: In year 2, first month, dingmao day, at Huojia he recalled Si'an's short rations the year before, demoted him to Liuzhou registrar, then exiled him to Yazhou and ordered his death.)〉

sentences.zh: 鄧季筠，宋州下邑人也。

translations.literal: Deng Jiyun was a native of Xiayi in Songzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Jiyun came from Xiayi in Songzhou.

sentences.zh: 少入黃巢軍，隸於太祖麾下。

translations.literal: In youth he entered Huang Chao's army; attached to the Founder's command.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he joined Huang Chao and later entered the Founder's service.

sentences.zh: 及太祖鎮汴，首署為牙將，主騎軍。

translations.literal: When the Founder held Bian he first appointed him as dental officer in charge of cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder held Bian he made Jiyun a personal guard officer commanding the cavalry.

sentences.zh: 伐鄆之役，生擒排陣將劉矯以獻。

translations.literal: In the Yan campaign he personally captured battle-array general Liu Jiao and presented him.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yan campaign he took the enemy battle-line general Liu Jiao alive and presented him.

sentences.zh: 唐大順初，唐帝命丞相張浚伐太原，太祖奉詔出師，西至高平，與晉人接戰，軍既不利，季筠為晉人所擒。

translations.literal: Tang Dashun early, Tang Emperor ordered Chancellor Zhang Jun to attack Taiyuan; the Founder received edict and marched; west to Gaoping, engaged Jin troops; the army was unfavorable; Jiyun was captured by Jin men.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Dashun of Tang, the emperor sent Chancellor Zhang Jun against Taiyuan; the Founder marched west to Gaoping, was beaten, and Jiyun was captured by the Jin.

sentences.zh: 克用見之甚喜，釋縛，待以賓禮，俄典戎事。

translations.literal: Keyong saw him and was greatly pleased, released his bonds, treated him as guest; soon put in charge of military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong was delighted, freed him, entertained him as a guest, and soon put him in charge of troops.

sentences.zh: 季筠在並門凡四稔。

translations.literal: Jiyun at Bing Gate altogether four years.
translations.idiomatic: Jiyun stayed at Taiyuan four years.

sentences.zh: 景福二年，晉軍攻邢台，季筠領偏師預其役，將及邢，邢人陣於郊，兩軍酣戰之際，季筠出陣，飛馬來歸；

translations.literal: Jingfu 2, Jin army attacked Xingtai; Jiyun led flank army sharing the campaign; about to reach Xing; Xing men arrayed at the suburbs; as the two armies fought hotly Jiyun left the line, on flying horse came back;
translations.idiomatic: In Jingfu 2 the Jin besieged Xingtai; Jiyun led a flank corps; as the armies fought outside Xing he broke from the line and galloped back to the Founder;

sentences.zh: 太祖大加獎歎，賞賚甚厚。

translations.literal: The Founder greatly praised and rewarded him richly.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder praised him lavishly and gave rich rewards.

sentences.zh: 時初置廳子都，最為親軍，命季筠主之，旋改統親騎，又遷將中軍。

translations.literal: At the time first established the Hall Sons army, most intimate troops; ordered Jiyun to command it; soon changed to command intimate cavalry; again promoted to command center army.
translations.idiomatic: He then formed the Hall Sons—the Founder's closest guard—and put Jiyun in command, soon made him head of the intimate cavalry and then of the central army.

sentences.zh: 天祐三年，奏授登州刺史，下車稱理。

translations.literal: Tianyou 3, memorialized as Dengzhou prefect; on taking office he was praised for good governance.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianyou 3 he became prefect of Dengzhou and governed well from the day he arrived.

sentences.zh: 登州舊無羅城，及季筠至郡，率丁壯以築之，民甚安之，因相與立碑以頌其績。

translations.literal: Dengzhou formerly had no outer wall; when Jiyun reached the prefecture he led strong young men to build it; the people were very at ease; therefore together they erected a stele to praise his merit.
translations.idiomatic: Dengzhou had no outer wall; Jiyun raised labor to build one, the people were secure, and they set up a stele to praise him.

sentences.zh: 太祖受禪，改鄭州刺史，尋主兵於河中，為都指揮使。

translations.literal: When the Founder received the mandate, changed to Zhengzhou prefect; soon commanded troops at Hezhong as overall commander.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of Liang he became prefect of Zhengzhou, then commanded the army at Hezhong as overall commander.

sentences.zh: 時並人寇平陽，季筠接戰於洪洞，大克，拜華州防禦使。

translations.literal: At the time Jin men raided Pingyang; Jiyun engaged at Hongdong and greatly overcame; made Huazhou defense commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin raided Pingyang he routed them at Hongdong and was made defense commissioner of Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 又繼領龍驤等諸軍騎士，累官至檢校司空。

translations.literal: Again successively commanded Longxiang and other army cavalry; repeatedly rose to Acting Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He later led the Longxiang and other cavalry corps and rose to Acting Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 柏鄉之役，季筠臨陣前卻，太祖亦未之罪。

translations.literal: At the Battle of Bai Bridge, Jiyun before the battle drew back; the Founder also did not blame him.
translations.idiomatic: At Bai Bridge Jiyun pulled back in the fighting, yet the Founder did not punish him.

sentences.zh: 乾化二年春，太祖親伐鎮、定，駐於相州，因閱馬，怒其馬瘦，與魏博軍校何令稠、陳令勳同斬於纛下。

translations.literal: Kaiping 2 spring, the Founder in person attacked Zhen and Ding, halted at Xiangzhou; because of reviewing horses he was angry their horses were thin and with Weibo army officers He Lingchou and Chen Lingxun alike cut them beneath the banner.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of Kaiping 2 the Founder attacked Zhen and Ding and halted at Xiangzhou; reviewing the horses, he found them lean and beheaded Jiyun with the Weibo officers He Lingchou and Chen Lingxun beneath his banner.

sentences.zh: 黃文靖，金鄉人。

translations.literal: Huang Wenjing was a native of Jinxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Wenjing came from Jinxiang.

sentences.zh: 少附於黃巢黨中，巢敗，歸於太祖，累署牙職，繼遷諸軍指揮使。

translations.literal: In youth he attached to Huang Chao's party; when Chao was defeated returned to the Founder; repeatedly appointed dental posts; successively promoted to army commanders.
translations.idiomatic: He had followed Huang Chao; after Chao's fall he joined the Founder, served in the guard corps, and rose to army commander.

sentences.zh: 從太祖南平巢、蔡，北定兗、鄆，皆有功。

translations.literal: Following the Founder south pacified Chao and Cai, north settled Yan and Yun—all had merit.
translations.idiomatic: He fought south against Chao and Cai and north in Yan and Yun, winning merit in each.

sentences.zh: 唐大順中，佐葛從周送朱崇節入潞。

translations.literal: Tang Dashun, assisted Ge Congzhou in escorting Zhu Chongjie into Lu.
translations.idiomatic: In Dashun of Tang he helped Ge Congzhou escort Zhu Chongjie into Lu.

sentences.zh: 會晉軍十餘萬近逼垣寨，文靖慮孤軍難守，乃與葛從周啟出師，文靖為殿，命矢刃皆外向，持重而還，晉人不敢逼。

translations.literal: Jin army over a hundred thousand pressed near the stockade; Wenjing feared lone army hard to hold; with Ge Congzhou secretly led troops out; Wenjing as rearguard ordered arrow blades all face outward, moved deliberately and returned; Jin men dared not press.
translations.idiomatic: When more than a hundred thousand Jin troops pressed the camp, Wenjing and Ge Congzhou slipped out by night; Wenjing covered the rear with weapons turned outward and withdrew in good order while the Jin held back.

sentences.zh: 其年冬，與康懷英渡淮，入壽春之境，下安豐、霍丘，至光州而還。

translations.literal: That winter with Kang Huaiying crossed Huai, entered Shouchun border, took Anfeng and Huoqiu, reached Guangzhou and returned.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he crossed the Huai with Kang Huaiying, took Anfeng and Huoqiu in Shouzhou, reached Guangzhou, and returned.

sentences.zh: 光化初，晉將李嗣昭、周德威寇於山東，文靖佐葛從周統大軍禦之。

translations.literal: Guanghua early, Jin generals Li Sizhao and Zhou Dewei raided Shandong; Wenjing assisted Ge Congzhou in commanding great army to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Guanghua, when Li Sizhao and Zhou Dewei raided Shandong, Wenjing joined Ge Congzhou in commanding the main army against them.

sentences.zh: 至沙河，敗晉軍五千餘騎，遂逐之，越張公橋乃止。

translations.literal: Reached Shahe, defeated Jin army over five thousand cavalry; pursued them past Zhanggong Bridge then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: At Shahe he routed more than five thousand Jin horsemen and pursued them past Zhanggong Bridge before halting.

sentences.zh: 後旬日，復與晉人戰於邢州之北，擒蕃將賁金鐵、慕容藤、李存建等百餘人，奪馬數千匹。

translations.literal: Ten days later again fought Jin at north of Xingzhou; captured Tatar generals Ben Jintie, Murong Teng, Li Cunjian and over a hundred men; seized horses several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Ten days later he fought again north of Xingzhou, capturing the Tatar generals Ben Jintie, Murong Teng, Li Cunjian, and more than a hundred others, with thousands of horses.

sentences.zh: 尋以功表授檢校左僕射、耀州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon for merit memorialized Acting Left Vice Director and Yaozhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was memorialized Acting Left Vice Director and prefect of Yaozhou.

sentences.zh: 天祐二年春，命佐楊師厚深入淮甸，越壽春，侵廬江，軍至大獨山，遇淮夷，殺五千餘眾，振旅而還。

translations.literal: Tianyou 2 spring, ordered to assist Yang Shihou in deep penetration Huai region; past Shouchun, invaded Lujiang; army reached Great Solitary Mountain; met Huai barbarians, killed over five thousand; army returned in triumph.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of Tianyou 2 he aided Yang Shihou deep into the Huai, passed Shouchun, raided Lujiang, reached Great Solitary Mountain, killed more than five thousand Huai fighters, and returned in triumph.

sentences.zh: 改蔡州刺史，加檢校司空，又遷潁州刺史。

translations.literal: Changed to Cai prefect; added Acting Minister of Works; again moved to Ying prefect.
translations.idiomatic: He became prefect of Cai with Acting Minister of Works, then moved to Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 太祖受禪，復為蔡州刺史，入為左神武統軍，又改左龍驤使。

translations.literal: When the Founder received the mandate, again Cai prefect; entered as Left Divine Martial overall commander; again changed to Left Dragon Flying commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: At the Liang founding he was again prefect of Cai, then Left Divine Martial commander and Left Dragon Flying commissioner.

sentences.zh: 乾化元年，從太祖北征，因閱馬得罪，命斬之。

translations.literal: Kaiping 1, followed Founder north campaign; because of horse review offended; ordered executed.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiping 1 he joined the northern campaign; the horse review angered the Founder and he was executed.

sentences.zh: 文靖驍果善戰，諸將皆惜之。

translations.literal: Wenjing was fierce and good in battle; all generals prized him.
translations.idiomatic: Wenjing was a fierce fighter whom every general regretted losing.

sentences.zh: 李讜，河中臨晉人。

translations.literal: Li Dang was a native of Linjin in Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dang came from Linjin in Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 少時遊秦、雍間，為人勇悍多力，甚有氣誼。

translations.literal: In youth he roamed Qin and Yong regions; as a man brave, fierce, and very strong, greatly had chivalrous friendship.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he wandered Qin and Yong; bold, fierce, and strong, he was famed for loyalty among friends.

sentences.zh: 唐廣明初，黃巢陷長安，讜遂得仕於其間。

translations.literal: Tang Guangming early, Huang Chao took Chang'an; Dang then obtained office among them.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Guangming of Tang, when Huang Chao took Chang'an, Dang entered his service.

sentences.zh: 巢以讜為內樞密使，蓋讜曾委質於宦者，出入於宮禁間，巢以此用焉。

translations.literal: Chao made Dang inner privy commissioner; because Dang had once placed himself under eunuchs and went in and out of palace confines—Chao used him thus.
translations.idiomatic: Chao made him inner privy commissioner, for Dang had once served eunuchs and knew the palace—Chao used him for that.

sentences.zh: 其後巢軍既敗，讜乃束身歸於太祖，署為左德勝騎軍都將。

translations.literal: After Chao's army was defeated Dang bound himself and returned to the Founder; appointed Left Victorious Virtue cavalry commander.
translations.idiomatic: After Chao's defeat Dang surrendered to the Founder and was made commander of the Left Victorious Virtue cavalry.

sentences.zh: 從太祖討蔡賊，頗立軍功。

translations.literal: Following the Founder against Cai bandits, considerably established military merit.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the Founder against the Cai rebels and won solid merit.

sentences.zh: 及東伐兗、鄆，以所部士伍俘獲甚眾，改元從騎將，表授檢校右僕射。

translations.literal: And east attacking Yan and Yun, with his command's soldiers captured very many; changed to yuancong cavalry general; memorialized Acting Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: In the eastern campaigns against Yan and Yun his men took many prisoners; he became a yuancong cavalry general and Acting Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 郴王友裕領兵攻澤州，時太祖駐大軍於盟津，乃令讜將兵越太行，授以籌謀。

translations.literal: Prince of Chen Youyu led troops to attack Zezhou; the Founder then stationed great army at Meng Ford; then ordered Dang to lead troops across Taihang; entrusted with planning.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Chen Youyu besieged Zezhou the Founder camped at Meng Ford and sent Dang across the Taihang with full discretion over the plan.

sentences.zh: 讜頗違節度，久而無功。

translations.literal: Dang quite violated command; for long had no merit.
translations.idiomatic: Dang disobeyed orders and after a long while had nothing to show.

sentences.zh: 太祖遣追還，廷責其罪，戮之於河橋。

translations.literal: The Founder sent to recall him; at court blamed his crime; executed him at He Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder recalled him, rebuked him at court, and executed him at He Bridge.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：叔琮而下，咸以鷹犬之才，適遇雲龍之會，勤勞王室，踐履將壇，然俱不得其死，豈不惜哉！

translations.literal: The historiographer says: From Shuzong down, all with hawk-and-hound talent met the cloud-dragon's conjunction; diligently served the royal house, trod the general's altar—yet all did not obtain their death; how is it not pitiable!
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: From Shuzong on, these men had the talent of hawks and hounds and met a dragon in the clouds; they toiled for the throne and stood on the general's dais—yet none died in his bed. How pitiable!

sentences.zh: 得非鳥盡弓藏，理當如是耶？

translations.literal: Is it not that when birds are gone bows are stored—reason ought to be thus?
translations.idiomatic: When the birds are gone, does not every lord put away his bow? Is that not fate?

sentences.zh: 將梁祖之雄猜，無漢高之大度歟？

translations.literal: Was the Liang Founder's heroic suspiciousness without Han Gaozu's great magnanimity?
translations.idiomatic: Was the Liang Founder's jealous courage so far below Han Gaozu's breadth of mind?

sentences.zh: 乃知自古帝王，能保全功臣者，唯光武一人而已矣。

translations.literal: Thus one knows from ancient emperors and kings, those who could wholly preserve meritorious ministers were only Guangwu alone!
translations.idiomatic: So of all emperors since antiquity, only Guangwu truly kept his merit ministers safe.

sentences.zh: 語曰：「弑父與君，亦不從也」，而叔琮、友恭從之，何也？

translations.literal: The saying goes: "Kill father and lord—yet also do not follow"; yet Shuzong and Yougong followed—why?
translations.idiomatic: The Analects says one must not obey even a father or lord in murder—yet Shuzong and Yougong obeyed. Why?

sentences.zh: 既為盜蹠所嗾，豈免成濟之誅，臨終之言，益彰其醜也。

translations.literal: Already driven by robber Zhi—how escape Cheng Ji punishment; words at life's end all the more reveal their ugliness.
translations.idiomatic: Urged on by a Zhi, they could only share Cheng Ji's fate; their dying words exposed their shame all the more.
